transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Time: 16:00 ET
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jamie Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (BlueCross CTO), Tanya Liu (BlueCross Platform), Sara Gomez (BlueCross Security), Alex (BlueCross Dev)

Auto-generated summary (brief): demo focused on rate limiting, quotas and multi-tenant controls using org and project keys. Walkthrough of Redwood Console policies, CLI examples, and discussion of pilot criteria and security concerns (KMS, audit logs, SSO).

[00:00] Jamie Ellis: hey everyone thanks for joining, im jamie from redwood, i'll kick things off, priya is our se and she'll run the console demo. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Mark Rivera: good thanks, loud office here but we're all set. main thing for today is to see how you do per-tenant limits and make sure we can map to our team keys and SSO.
[00:14] Jamie: perfect. quick agenda — show org vs project keys, per-key rate limits, quotas, burst behaviors, how to set limits per-route, and then a short Q&A about security and pilot steps.
[00:28] Priya Shah: i'll share my screen — lmk if the console is visible.
[00:35] Tanya Liu: yep seeing it.
[00:38] Priya: cool. so this is the Redwood Console, top nav has org settings, billing, and projects. first thing i want to show is org-level policy. you can create policies that apply across all projects — common for enterprise tenants. here we have a policy named "bluecross-org-default" set to 1000 req/min total with token-bucket burst of 200.
[01:05] Alex: when you say req/min is that per-second smoothing? how strict is the enforcement — are there headers returned so our client can backoff?
[01:12] Priya: yes, we send standard ratelimit headers (x-ratelimit-limit, x-ratelimit-remaining, x-ratelimit-reset). enforcement is token-bucket so you'll see bursts allowed up to configured capacity and then steady-state throttling. sometimes the header names differ slightly in our hosted mode but that's the pattern.
[01:28] Sara Gomez: is the token-bucket state stored per-project or per-key? we need to ensure noisy neighbor protection within projects.
[01:34] Priya: good question. in Redwood we support both: you can scope the bucket to org-level, project-level or individual API keys. typically for noisy neighbor protection you scope per-project or per-key. the console UI shows policy scope dropdown.
[01:50] Jamie: one nuance — for dedicated and private deployments we also support cluster-local enforcement which reduces cross-region races.
[01:58] Mark: what about per-route limits? we have a couple of heavy endpoints (e.g., /chat/stream and embeddings) that we want lower limits for than generic generation.
[02:06] Priya: yep we have per-route rules. i'll open the rule editor — here we have a rule for "/v1/generate/chat" set to 50 rps per project while embeddings are 20 rps. you can stack rules, and order matters (first-match wins).
[02:22] Alex: can rules be set based on model variant? like smaller models vs bigger ones?
[02:27] Priya: yes, rules support attributes — model name, model size tag, region, and header matches. so you can say if model==redwood-2-large then limit differently.
[02:36] Tanya: from a quota perspective, do you do monthly token quotas per project? we need spend controls tied to teams.
[02:42] Priya: absolutely — quotas are separate from rate limits. quotas are token-based (or request-based) with reset windows (monthly default). you can set soft limits (warn) and hard limits (block). the console shows usage burn rate and projected exhaustion.
[02:55] Mark: that projected burn is helpful. can we export that to our billing system?
[03:00] Jamie: we have APIs and webhooks for usage export; during pilot we usually provide CSV exports and a webhook integration for near-real-time events.
[03:08] Sara: security: where are these policies stored and who can edit them? we need RBAC tied to SSO groups.
[03:14] Priya: policies live in the control plane. RBAC supports roles at org and project levels, and we integrate with SAML SSO and SCIM for group sync. only users with "policy_admin" role can edit limits; audit logs record all changes.
[03:30] Sara: are logs tamper-evident? we have auditors asking about immutable audit trails.
[03:36] Jamie: we integrate with customer KMS for signing, and we can ship logs to your SIEM (syslog, S3, or a partner). for private deployments you can also enable HSM.
[03:46] Mark: curious on how enforcement behaves on degraded infra — fallback strategy?
[03:50] Priya: by default we prefer graceful degradation: you can set fallback policies to route to a cheaper model, degrade throughput, or serve cached responses. It's configurable per-route. for strict SLOs you can pin to dedicated capacity.
[04:05] Alex: demo question — can i create project keys via API? we want to auto-provision keys for new teams.
[04:10] Priya: yes, projects and keys are first-class in the API. quick curl: curl -X POST /v1/orgs/{org}/projects -d '{"name":"team-a"}' then create API key. the response includes key metadata and you can attach policy ids. (note: sample shows escaped JSON)
[04:28] Jamie: i want to show a short example of per-key throttling. priya will switch to the traffic simulator.
[04:34] Priya: switching — this sim pushes requests at 500 rps and you can see the project's bucket drain, then enforcement kicks in and you get 429s with x-retry-after header. sometimes the transcriber shows 42 nine as 4 29, sorry, that's a transcription quirk.
[04:50] [simulator noise in recording] 
[04:58] Mark: those 429s look fine. do you provide client SDKs that automatically backoff?
[05:04] Priya: we offer client-side SDKs with exponential backoff helpers and a small JS library that parses headers.
[05:09] Tanya: talk about org vs project key billing — we want team owners to own budgets. can spend be routed to project-level billing or consolidated?
[05:16] Jamie: yes, consolidated billing is default but you can enable project-level chargeback and export tags for chargeback. we surface cost per-route and per-key in Redwood Optimize — that helps teams see where tokens are heavy.
[05:28] Alex: earlier you mentioned prefix caching and KV cache. how does that interplay with rate limits? cached responses shouldn't count toward quotas ideally. is that supported?
[05:36] Priya: good call — we support cache-safe rules: if a response is served from cache, you can choose whether it counts toward quota. defaults vary by deployment; hosted mode may count reads differently. we'll surface this config in the policy editor.
[05:53] Sara: compliance question — can policy changes be scoped to a change window and require approvals? we need two-person approval for Prod policy changes.
[06:00] Priya: yes, we have a policy change workflow with approvals, and a changelog with diff view. you can require reviewer groups.
[06:08] Mark: what's the limit granularity — per-second, per-minute, per-hour?
[06:12] Priya: we support per-second (rps), per-minute, and sliding window token buckets. quotas support arbitrary windows (e.g. 30-day rolling).
[06:20] Alex: latency impact — does token-bucket enforcement add latency?
[06:23] Priya: negligible — it's done in the control plane at the ingress layer. in dedicated/private you can run enforcement co-located to avoid additional RTT.
[06:32] Jamie: i'll quickly click to the policies export — you can export JSON for IaC. here's an example snippet (simplified):
{
  "policy_id":"p-12345",
  "scope":"project",
  "limits":{
    "rate":50,
    "burst":100,
    "window":"1s"
  }
} 
(note: in real export there are metadata fields, encrypted key refs, etc — console truncates for view)
[06:58] Tanya: will you share a real export? we want to evaluate applying it to our terraform.
[07:03] Priya: yes — next steps i will attach the full export and screenshots.
[07:08] Mark: pilot logistics — we're targeting a mid-January pilot with two teams, ~200 rps aggregate, peak 500, mixed chat and embeddings. are those numbers doable on hosted or should we go dedicated?
[07:18] Jamie: for that profile hosted can probably handle with smart routing and burst capacity, but if you need guaranteed low tail latency and isolation for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private with dedicated GPU pools. we'll include a capacity/price estimate in the pilot doc.
[07:32] Sara: PHI — we will not send PHI to a multi-tenant hosted environment without a BAA. what are your options?
[07:40] Jamie: we sign a BAA for enterprise contracts and we offer Private deployments for strict data residency. Dedicated is also an option if isolation plus managed control plane is acceptable.
[07:48] Alex: any gotchas on API key rotation? we want short-lived keys for safety.
[07:52] Priya: we support short-lived keys and automatic rotation; there is an API for creating ephemeral keys via a service principal.
[07:59] Mark: ok this is super helpful. quick question on observability — do you show per-key traces and latency percentiles?
[08:06] Priya: yes, Redwood Console has per-route, per-model and per-key dashboards — p50/p95/p99, token breakdown by prompt/response, and trace links to our distributed tracing.
[08:18] Jamie: i'm going to summarize next steps — priya will send configs and screenshots; i'll send pilot pricing and security docs including SOC2/BAA info; mark you'll send traffic profile. then we circle back to scope the POC.
[08:30] Mark: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:33] Sara: thanks.
